editorial:
Imagine walking into a police station and admitting you killed your wife. That is exactly how you start this story. You meet Soichiro Kaji, a retired cop who claims he killed his wife because she had Alzheimer's and wanted to die. It sounds like a sad, straightforward case, but there is a huge catch. Kaji has a 48-hour gap in his story that he cannot explain. The movie starts off feeling like a tense crime mystery, but it quickly turns into a deep look at love, guilt, and what it means to do the right thing. The mood is quiet and heavy, making you feel the weight of the characters' sadness.

What really makes this work is the acting. The lead actor plays the role of the grieving husband perfectly, keeping you guessing about his true motives. While the pace is a bit slow at times, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you enjoy stories that focus more on people than on loud action, you will love this. To get the best experience, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for those crisp visuals. It is a great pick for a rainy night when you want something meaningful.
endingExplained: You eventually find out that Kaji did not actually kill his wife. He only confessed to the crime to protect someone else and to find a way to deal with his own grief. The twist reveals the true sequence of events during those missing 48 hours, showing that his confession was an act of love and sacrifice. In the end, the truth comes out, and the movie wraps up by focusing on forgiveness and peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and sad mysteries.
